content.text: The text reviews acute and chronic intestinal catarrh, cholera morbus, summer diarrhoea, cholera infantum, and pseudo-membranous enteritis. It details causes including irritant poisons, contaminated food or water, alcohol, parasites, emotional stress, poor hygiene, heat, and unsuitable infant feeding. Pathology includes intestinal hyperaemia, oedema, mucus, follicular enlargement, ulceration, atrophy, and occasionally perforation. Symptoms range from colicky pain and watery, mucous, or bloody stools to vomiting, fever, dehydration, wasting, collapse, and neurological complications. Diagnosis relies on stool character, disease course, distribution of lesions, and differentiation from typhoid, dysentery, poisoning, and peritonitis. Treatment emphasizes rest, carefully regulated diet, clean air, hydration, breastfeeding or suitable milk, digestive aids, bismuth, cautious opiates, rectal therapy, and climate change. Sandra journeyed to the kitchen.
